blocks.text: There are two types of vector multiplication; their products are known as the scalar product and the vector product.

blocks.title: Scalar and vector products
blocks.text: If the product of two vectors results in a scalar quantity it is called the scalar product, while if the product of two vectors results in a vector quantity it is called the vector product.

The scalar product of two vectors A and B is written A.B and is defined as A.B = A B cos theta ... (2.6), where A and B are the magnitudes of the vectors and theta is the angle between them. For the physical interpretation, the two vectors are first brought to a common origin (Fig. 2.2a); then A.B = A (projection of B on A), or A.B = A (magnitude of the component of B in the direction of A) = A (B cos theta) = AB cos theta (Fig. 2.2b). Similarly B.A = B (A cos theta) = BA cos theta.

blocks.alt: Two panels. (a) Vector A lies along the base; vector B rises at angle theta; a dashed line drops from the tip of B to A, and the shaded piece of A up to that point is labelled B cos theta. (b) The same angle; a dashed line from the tip of A meets B at a right angle, and the piece of B up to that point is labelled A cos theta.
blocks.caption: Dot product: projection of B on A (a) and of A on B (b) (original diagram after Figure 2.2).

blocks.text: We come across this product when we consider the work done by a force F whose point of application moves a distance d in a direction making an angle theta with the line of action of F (Fig. 2.3): work done = (effective component of force in the direction of motion) x distance moved = (F cos theta) d = F d cos theta; in vector notation, F.d = F d cos theta = work done.

blocks.alt: A block on a floor is pulled by a red force F at angle theta above the horizontal. A blue arrow along the floor shows its component F cos theta, a green arrow below shows the displacement d, and a box gives W = (F cos theta) d = F . d.
blocks.caption: A force F at angle theta moves a block through d: work = F d cos theta (original diagram after Figure 2.3).

items: Since A.B = AB cos theta and B.A = BA cos theta = AB cos theta, A.B = B.A: the order of multiplication is irrelevant, the scalar product is commutative.
The scalar product of two mutually perpendicular vectors (theta = 90 degrees) is zero: A.B = AB cos 90 = 0.

The scalar product of two parallel vectors equals the product of their magnitudes: for parallel vectors (theta = 0) A.B = AB cos 0 = AB; for antiparallel vectors (theta = 180 degrees) A.B = AB cos 180 = -AB. The self product of a vector equals the square of its magnitude: A.A = AA cos 0 = A^2.

In terms of rectangular components, A.B = Ax Bx + Ay By + Az Bz ... (2.7). Equation (2.6) then gives the angle between two vectors: since A.B = AB cos theta = Ax Bx + Ay By + Az Bz, cos theta = (Ax Bx + Ay By + Az Bz) / (AB) ... (2.8).

blocks.text: The vector product of two vectors A and B is a vector defined as A x B = AB sin theta n-hat ... (2.9), where n-hat is a unit vector perpendicular to the plane containing A and B (Fig. 2.4a). Its direction is found by the right-hand rule: place the tails of A and B together to define their plane; the direction of the product vector is perpendicular to this plane; rotate the first vector A into B through the smaller of the two possible angles and curl the fingers of the right hand in the direction of rotation, keeping the thumb erect; the direction of the product vector is along the erect thumb (Fig. 2.4b). Because of this rule, B x A is a vector opposite in sign to A x B (Fig. 2.4c); hence A x B = -B x A ... (2.10).

items: Since A x B is not the same as B x A, the cross product is non-commutative: A x B is not equal to B x A.
The cross product of two perpendicular vectors (theta = 90 degrees) has maximum magnitude: A x B = AB sin 90 n-hat = AB n-hat.
The cross product of two parallel vectors is the null vector, because for such vectors theta = 0 or 180 degrees, so A x B = AB sin 0 n-hat = 0 or AB sin 180 n-hat = 0; as a consequence A x A = 0.
The magnitude of A x B equals the area of the parallelogram formed with A and B as two adjacent sides (Fig. 2.4d).

When a force F is applied on a rigid body at a point whose position vector is r from any point on the axis about which the body rotates, the turning effect of the force, the torque tau, is given by the vector product of r and F: tau = r x F.
The force F on a particle of charge q and velocity v in a magnetic field of strength B is given by the vector product of v and B: F = q (v x B).

blocks.alt: Four panels. (a) Vectors A and B lie in a plane with angle theta between them; A x B points straight up from the plane. (b) Right-hand rule: fingers curl from A to B and the thumb gives A x B. (c) The same plane with B x A pointing straight down, equal to minus A x B. (d) A and B form a parallelogram whose area AB sin theta equals the size of A x B.
blocks.caption: Cross product: A x B, the right-hand rule, B x A and the parallelogram area (original diagram after Figure 2.4).
